result: Probed libcst.metadata.QualifiedNameProvider behavior on 6 minimal snippets (simple import, dotted-submodule import, aliased import, from-import-as, param-shadowed name with no import, reassigned-local shadowing an import) via a CSTVisitor with METADATA_DEPENDENCIES=(QualifiedNameProvider,); confirmed: usage-site Name leaves equal to old_root resolve to QualifiedNameSource.IMPORT with name either exactly old_root (bare/dotted-submodule import) or old_root.<subpath> (from-import), while shadowed locals/params resolve to QualifiedNameSource.LOCAL, alias-bound names (rt, P) resolve via IMPORT but their own text is not old_root so they are correctly left untouched, attribute-position Names (foo.runtime.bar) and keyword-argument Names resolve to an empty qualified-name set, and string literals/comment text are never visited as Name nodes at all -- confirming strings/comments/attribute-position/shadowed-local exclusion is achieved by construction via scope resolution, with no textual special-casing required. Implemented tools/refactor_repo/rewrite_runtime_imports.py (_RuntimeImportRewriter(cst.CSTTransformer) + rewrite_source()/scan_residuals() API + CLI dry-run/apply/postcondition-scan driver) on this basis, pinned to libcst==1.8.2 via importlib.metadata.version() assertion at import time (raises RuntimeError otherwise). Manually exercised 15 inline cases covering every required fixture class: simple_import, aliased_import, dotted_submodule_import, multiline_from_import (parens+inline comment preserved verbatim), from_import_aliased_module, string_literal_non_target, comment_non_target, dynamic_import_literal (diagnostic emitted, content unchanged), dynamic_import_computed (unsafe diagnostic, file unmodified), ambiguous_shadowed_param (non_target_shadowed diagnostic, unmodified), ambiguous_shadowed_reassign (import line rewritten, shadowed local body left untouched), already_migrated (zero diagnostics, unchanged), malformed_python (parse_error diagnostic, unsafe, unmodified, no crash), mixed_old_new (both target the same result, duplicate_import_after_rewrite warning emitted), relative_import_non_target (from . import / from .runtime import both left untouched, zero diagnostics). All 15 matched the designed expected behavior on first run after fixing one bug (libcst version probe used undefined name 'libcst' instead of the 'cst' import alias; switched to importlib.metadata.version('libcst')). Also verified determinism (two rewrite_source() calls on identical input produce byte-identical output) and idempotence (re-running rewrite_source() on its own output produces changed=False) on the mixed_old_new case, and confirmed scan_residuals() reports zero residual_old_reference diagnostics on that case's post-rewrite output.
